entries.title: Zone F enemies: a chaser cell mid-mitosis while vault claws uncoil from the living wall
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. Inside the Cell Vault, a corridor grown rather than built: walls of pulsing green cells in a deep moss-to-jade ramp, fleshy folds ribbing the ceiling, pores blinking slow amber light, the whole organism breathing. Two threats dominate the mid-field. A CHASER CELL — a fist-tight sphere of translucent green membrane with a brighter dividing nucleus glowing inside — caught at the ugliest half-second of MITOSIS: the sphere waist-pinched into a dumbbell, two nuclei pulling apart on a spindle of pale filaments, the stretched membrane bridging them, about to become two hunters that will each remember where the player ran. Behind and below it, a VAULT CLAW erupting from the living wall: an eight-link tentacle hook of segmented bone-white plates wrapped in green tissue, each joint sparking a bead of fluid, the great curved talisman tip raking the air in a grab-arc that trails the fighter's last position. Lower left, a sleek steel-blue dart fighter with bold blue hull stripe and cyan canopy skims away hard, orange engine flare smearing along the membrane floor, pink and magenta round shots with bright cores and dark rims leaking from the pores around it, one purple spore-burst blooming where a claw-tip struck rock. Deep-navy shadow wells in the tissue folds, never pure black.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, human figures, cartoon mascot, soft pastel palette, red gore, exposed muscle, mechanical gears, wings on the cell
entries.notes: The mitosis pinch is the hero beat — it explains the chaser's split mechanic in one silhouette. Keep the vault green ramp (color reference #2a4434→#385a44) clearly plant-flesh, not blood: negatives ban gore deliberately. Claw reads as bone-plated tendril, eight links if the model can count, otherwise "clearly multi-segmented."

entries.title: Zone F enemies: a drift of chaser cells filling the vault chamber while a claw hauls a tender through the wall
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, ultrawide panoramic arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow. A vast organ-hall of the Cell Vault stretched across a panoramic frame: opposite walls of breathing green cell-mesh in a moss-to-jade ramp, ceiling ribbed with fleshy folds dripping slow amber beads, floor a soft membrane plain dimpled where things have landed. The hall is filling with CHASER CELLS — dozens of translucent green membrane spheres with hot pale nuclei, drifting in a slow convection current like an incoming tide, several caught mid-division as pinched dumbbells with spindles of filament strung between two nuclei, each pair already angling toward the same side of frame. In the right third, a VAULT CLAW — an eight-link bone-plated tentacle hook sheathed in green tissue — is hauled fully out of its wall socket, its joints leaking fluid beads, dragging a damaged mechanical TENDER drone through the torn membrane: the wide flat-bellied carrier sparkles with green coolant, belly hatch popped, and a stream of small pink-core shots spilling from it like escaping seed. At the far left edge a lone steel-blue dart fighter with cyan canopy and orange engine glow banks out of frame, the entire drift turning with it. Deep-navy shadow wells swallow the hall's ends, never pure black; one violet spore-glow pulses at each torn socket.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, human figures, cartoon mascot, soft pastel palette, red gore, duplicate fighter, extra player ships, bubbles underwater
entries.notes: The "incoming tide" version of the chase — scale horror instead of moment horror. The claw hauling a tender shows the vault's immune logic (it recaptures its own machines). Keep cells clearly spherical with visible nuclei; if the model starts making amoeba blobs, raise CFG slightly on sd3.5.

entries.title: Zone F enemies: portrait throat of the vault, cells raining down past a claw arch as the fighter climbs
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, vertical poster composition looking up the throat of a living structure, subtle CRT scanline glow. The frame is the inside of a great vertical gullet of the Cell Vault: circular walls of pulsing green cell-mesh in a moss-to-jade ramp narrowing upward, ringed with fleshy valve folds that stand half-open, pores shining amber down the whole height, the far top a pinprick of pale light. Raining down through the throat in a slow spiral, a swarm of CHASER CELLS: translucent membrane spheres with hot pale nuclei, dozens of them, many pinched mid-mitosis into dumbbells trailing spindle filaments that whip like sparks of pale thread, the closest ones large and soft-edged at the frame borders, the distant ones a scatter of green beads. Crossing the lower third, a VAULT CLAW anchored in the right wall has hooked the throat like an archer's brace — eight bone-plated segments sheathed in green tissue, each joint beading fluid, the massive curved tip pointing up the swarm's column. At the bottom of the frame, tiny, a steel-blue dart fighter with bold blue stripe, cyan canopy and a bright orange engine trail climbs straight into it, vapor snapping off its wings, pink and magenta shots with bright cores falling around it like ember-rain. Deep-navy pools ring the throat wall, never pure black; the valve folds pulse with one synchronized violet glow.
entries.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, watermark, blurry, pure black background, human figures, cartoon mascot, soft pastel palette, red gore, duplicate fighter, tentacle monster face, teeth in the wall
entries.notes: Ascent-poster version of the descent the player actually fights (Zone F runs horizontally, but the vault's vertical gullets are its signature architecture). The claw-as-brace gives the spiral a fulcrum. Watch that wall folds don't read as a monstrous mouth — ban teeth in the negative.

entries.title: In-game pixel sprite sheet: POLYP TURRET firing states, four frames on key green
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art, flat colored pixel sprites with crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines and simple two-tone dithered shading, arranged as a regular grid of four equal cells in two rows of two, read left to right and top to bottom, on a completely flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, one firing state per cell, the same polyp at the same scale, position and light in every cell, no scenery, no glow bleeding into the background, no text, no labels, no UI. Subject: the POLYP TURRET — a fleshy green wall-polyp fixed to a tissue base, vault greens #2a4434→#385a44. Four frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: closed bud, swelling bud, blooming mouth, and the discharged puff after release. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the firing state changes. Chunky readable arcade silhouettes, saturated limited palette, crisp pixel-grid edges, every sprite facing left.
entries.negative: text, labels, letters, numbers, watermark, photograph, 3d render, smooth gradients, anti-aliased, glow on background, scenery, flat background replaced, fused sprites, overlapping sprites, red blood, pure black background, perspective distortion, green tint on the subject, green spill, background scenery, cast shadow
entries.notes: The polyp's four firing states read the discharge cycle. The floating violet spore pixels, the pink and magenta bright-core round shots and the green rupture burst are pattern and particle material, not turret art — keep them off the sheet (bible §5.4, §6); the twin polyp sharing one base is this bud composed twice, not a third subject. The mitosis crown jewel lives on this file's filmstrip sheet. Vault greens #2a4434→#385a44; spores stay violet so they never read as blood. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: Square pixel sprite sheet: VAULT CLAW grab cycle, five frames on key green
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art, flat colored pixel sprites with crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines and simple two-tone dithered shading, arranged as a square sprite sheet — a regular grid of five equal cells in one row, read left to right, on a completely flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, one pose per cell, the same claw at the same scale, position and light in every cell, no scenery, no text, no labels, no UI. Subject: the VAULT CLAW — a bone-white eight-link grab hook on beaded joints, seated in a green tissue socket bump, the tentacle grab of the Cell Vault. Five frames, side view facing left. The frames in order: idle curl in the socket, reaching forward, hooked-in, hauling upward, and shattered at the third link with tissue fraying. Identical silhouette and palette in every cell — only the pose or damage state changes. Chunky arcade silhouettes, saturated limited palette, crisp pixel-grid edges, every sprite facing left.

entries.notes: The socket bump is part of the claw; the two falling bone fragments are a hand-cleanup debris note and the fluid droplet beads belong to the particle set (bible §6), never extra subjects on the sheet. The cell size ladder (grandmother → seed bead) and its damage states ride the filmstrip sheet as hand-scaled variants, and the spore-pattern row was always pattern-DSL reference for pattern authors, not art. This was the most "system sheet" of the zone sheets — one subject each keeps it triage-able. v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.

entries.title: Wide strip pixel sprite sheet: CHASER CELL division cycle, six frames on key green
entries.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art, flat colored pixel sprites with crisp 1-pixel near-black navy outlines and simple two-tone dithered shading, arranged as a wide horizontal filmstrip of six equal cells in one row, read left to right, on a completely flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background, one division state per cell, no scenery, no glow bleeding into the background, no text, no labels, no UI. Subject: the CHASER CELL — a round translucent green membrane sphere with a pale nucleus, the only enemy in the game whose sprite sheet doubles as a tutorial. Six frames, always the same round membrane silhouette and pale nucleus color with only the state changing, facing left. The frames in order: rest, nucleus elongating, membrane waisting into a dumbbell with a filament bridge, pinch to two touching daughters, daughters drifting apart each pulsing once, and the two settled independents facing left. Saturated limited palette, crisp pixel-grid edges, large readable clusters.

entries.notes: Continuity clause again — the same round membrane silhouette, only the state changing, is load-bearing; check it first when triaging. The "human anatomy" negative guards against the strip drifting into biology-textbook style: keep it arcade-cell, not microscope-cell. The claw extension strip is not this sheet's subject (it lives on the square sheet); the spore pixels, round shots, fluid droplet and rupture burst are effects and pattern material (bible §5.4, §6). v2 (R3-01): K3 key background #00FF00 — the ingest keys it by flood fill from the border, so greens inside the outline survive; frame counts follow the kernel's v2 targets.
